title: Tilted $p$-wave magnet candidate CeNiAsO
authors: Zhuo Wang, Zheng Liu, Shuo Zou, Hua-Xun Li, Jin-Xin Hu, Zhuolun Qiu, Ze Wang, Jiamin Gong, Lucheng Wei, Kangjian Luo, Hai Zeng, Meng Zhang, Chao Dong, Chuanyin Xi, Junfeng Wang, Jiakun Fang, Xiaotao Han, Guang-Han Cao, Liang Li, Yongkang Luo
abstract: The unexpectedly small ordered moments of CeNiAsO, a candidate for correlated $p$-wave magnet, have posed a serious challenge to the precise determination of its magnetic structure, hindering the understanding of its fundamental properties. By leveraging the high sensitivity to local internal fields, our $^{75}$As nuclear quadrupole / magnetic resonance experiments reveal a commensurate antiferromagnetic order with a small out-of-plane moment $m_z\approx0.05$ $μ_{\mathrm{B}}$. This tilted magnetic configuration not only rotates the spin polarization axis away from the crystallographic $\mathbf{c}$-axis, but also enhances the non-relativistic spin splitting. We refer to this rare paradigm as a \textit{tilted $p$-wave magnet}.
summary: This work determines the magnetic structure of CeNiAsO, identifying it as a 'tilted p-wave magnet' based on NQR/NMR measurements. The study establishes a commensurate, non-collinear antiferromagnetic order characterized by a small out-of-plane moment. By combining spectroscopy and transport measurements, the authors provide strong evidence for this exotic magnetic state in a heavy-fermion compound.
main_problem: The magnetic structure of CeNiAsO, a candidate for a correlated p-wave magnet, is difficult to determine due to its unexpectedly small ordered magnetic moments.
main_result: The study reveals a commensurate antiferromagnetic order with a small, non-collinear, out-of-plane moment, characterizing the material as a 'tilted p-wave magnet'.
method: The research combines high-sensitivity $^{75}	ext{As}$ NQR/NMR experiments to probe local internal fields with DFT+U calculations to model electronic structure and anomalous transport.
model_or_system: The system is CeNiAsO, which exhibits two sequential antiferromagnetic transitions. The magnetic state is modeled as a tilted-coplanar commensurate AFM order, analyzed using a total Hamiltonian incorporating quadrupole and interaction terms.
key_observables: Internal magnetic field ($\mathbf{B}_{	ext{int}}$), NQR/NMR peak splitting, Anomalous Hall Effect ($ho_{Axy}$), and spin splitting ($\Delta S$).
important_parameters: Small out-of-plane moment ($m_z \approx 0.05 \mu_B$), $\mathbf{B}_{	ext{int}} \approx 0.213 	ext{ T}$, and the canting angle $	heta_{	ext{int}} \approx 44^\circ$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the magnetic structure is dominated by the commensurate AFM phase and that the internal field can be accurately determined via hyperfine coupling measurements.
figures_summary: Figures show NQR/NMR spectra fitting the internal field orientation ($	heta_{	ext{int}} \approx 44^\circ$), the emergence of AHE loops in $ho_{yx}$ at low T, and calculations confirming the coplanar nature of the magnetic moments.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by using NQR/NMR to pinpoint the internal field and magnetic canting angle, followed by DFT+U calculations to confirm the electronic consequences, and finally analyzing the AHE in transport measurements to solidify the p-wave magnetic character.
why_interesting: The detailed characterization of the magnetic symmetry breaking and the resulting spin-orbit coupling effects, particularly the enhancement of spin splitting, provides a rich playground for understanding emergent quantum phenomena in strongly correlated systems.
